REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - SEPTEMBER 26, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to approve or ratify travel expenses for City-related business or to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR

2024, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Bishop David Montgomery, Church of Jesus Christ Latter-
  day Saints.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by representatives of the following youth sports
  organizations: AYSO Region 54; Cerritos Aquatic Club; Cerritos Girls Softball
  Association; Cerritos US Volleyball League; City of Cerritos Recreation Services Division
  Youth Sports volunteer coaches and players (basketball, soccer, and track); Frontier
  Youth Baseball League; Housh Enterprise/Snoop and Housh Football League; and Pacific
  Diving Academy.

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce W. Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  CTA Travel (Business Spotlight).

  Volleyball League; City of Cerritos Recreation Services Division Youth Sports volunteer
  coaches and players (basketball, soccer, and track); Frontier Youth Baseball League;
  Housh Enterprise/Snoop and Housh Football League; and Pacific Diving Academy
  (National Youth Sports Week).

  comments were submitted for meeting items by the deadline listed on the agenda.

  listed under Item 7A.1. Approval of the September 5, 2024 Council meeting minutes.
  The correct meeting time would be captured on the September 26, 2024 City
  Council/Successor Agency Meeting minutes document (Item 7A.1.).

7B.2. Approval of Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to authorize administrative

  Account/Project: 110-366-61340 (Outside Services)
  Amount:  $159,100 (Transfer)
  Justification: The Department of Public Works requests a budget amendment to
  cover the costs associated with emergency repairs at Gridley Park. On May 28, 2024,
  the department responded to a major 20-inch reclaimed water main break at the park.

  restoration of the backyard at 11620 Christy Avenue, which was affected by the incident
  (COUNCIL).

  transparency* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines, this project is exempt from CEQA review.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to:

  1. Authorize a Professional Services Agreement ("Agreement") with Tyler Technologies
  in the amount of $581,566;

  2. Authorize a Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25 budget amendment to establish a new capital
  project for the Enterprise Resource Planning software upgrade with an appropriation
  of $800,000. The appropriation includes both contractual expenses and anticipated

  use of $400,000 in General Fund reserves derived from the project's unused
  allocation in the FY 2023-24 operating budget and the reallocation of $400,000 that
  was budgeted and approved as part of the FY 2024-25 operating budget; and

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to direct staff to prepare an
  agenda report presenting a resolution for City Council review and consideration, prior to
  November 4, 2024, to place the proposed measure no. 2, to conduct a comprehensive
  “clean-up” and modernization of the City Charter on the Tuesday, March 4, 2025
  Cerritos General Municipal Election ballot, containing the ballot label, as listed below:

  Shall the Cerritos City Charter be amended to remove or modify provisions based
  on superseding and preemptive State law, increase Citywide operational
  efficiency by eliminating references to outdated business practices, and correct
  grammatical, punctuation, and spelling errors?

  ; (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to direct staff to prepare an
  agenda report presenting a resolution for City Council review and consideration, prior to
  November 4, 2024, to place the proposed measure no. 1, to require voter approval for
  any future changes to the City’s general municipal election date and related conforming
  amendments on the Tuesday, March 4, 2025 Cerritos General Municipal Election ballot,
  containing the ballot label, as listed below:

  Shall the Cerritos City Charter be amended to require that voter approval must be
  obtained for any future change to the City’s general municipal election date,
  currently established as the first Tuesday after the first Monday in March of each
  odd-numbered year, and make conforming amendments to the start date of each
  City Council member’s term and selection date of the Mayor, relating thereto?

  ; (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 - 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Johnson, Yokoyama

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

  renovation, would be reopening in October, 2024, and thanked the Parks and

  City staff:

  Communications Division: 27th Annual STAR Awards hosted by California Association of
  Public Information Officials (CAPIO) and States of California and Nevada Chapter of the
  National Association of Telecommunications Officers and Advisors (SCAN NATOA)
  (2nd Place - Parks & Recreation Category Video: Mayor's Weekly 60 - Week of March 4,
  2024; and 3rd Place - Arts & Entertainment Category Video: Mayor's Weekly 60 - Week
  of January 29, 2024).

  Management Information Systems Division: Municipal Information Systems Association
  of California (MISAC) (2024 Award for Excellence in Information Technology Practices).

  Additionally, Robert A. Lopez, City Manager, introduced Alvin Papa, the City’s new
  Director of Public Works/City Engineer.
